definitions.explanation: A compound word referring collectively to Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines. Used when discussing both types of religious sites together.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}には{寺社|じしゃ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many temples and shrines in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}には{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{寺社|じしゃ}を{訪|おとず}れる。
examples.english: Many people visit temples and shrines during the New Year.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}の{歴史的|れきしてき}な{寺社|じしゃ}を{巡|めぐ}るツアーに{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I joined a tour visiting the historic temples and shrines of this area.

notes:
USAGE:
The order {寺社|じしゃ} (temple-shrine) is the standard form. The reversed form {社寺|しゃじ} also exists and is interchangeable. Both refer to Buddhist temples ({寺|てら}) and Shinto shrines ({神社|じんじゃ}) collectively.

In historical contexts, {寺社|じしゃ}{奉行|ぶぎょう} was a Tokugawa-era magistrate overseeing temples and shrines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寺社|じしゃ}{仏閣|ぶっかく}: temples and shrines (more formal synonym)
- {寺社|じしゃ}{巡|めぐ}り: pilgrimage to temples and shrines
- {寺社|じしゃ}{奉行|ぶぎょう}: magistrate of temples and shrines (historical)
